Considering the legality of those sort of places in most of the U.S., do you have trouble finding them?

I wrote a guide on my subverse on finding MPs, but there's a couple different layers to address.

First, there are websites and forums that are dedicated to the hobby and provide mongers with reviews of various spas. These sites are good and bad. In a good way, it does provide valuable information to hobbyists on the quality of service, costs, locations, etc. In a bad way, it provides LE (law enforcement) with targets. Some will post sexually explicit information which endangers the MP to the extent that some mama-sans (female manager of the spa) request that users do not post reviews.

On these sites there are also mongers that will exchange private information on spas that aren't listed or where information is not readily available. One of my places in NYC is not known, but a fellow monger encouraged me to see this particular provider which was, literally, a life-changing experience.

As /u/JeffCrossley points out, there are also places that are easily identifiable by sight. Whether it's a strip mall shop with the neon "Open" sign or one of a half-dozen KMPs with awnings on 34th street in Manhattan, you'll see them.

Edit: Massage places aren't in and of themselves illegal. Generally, the act of a provider touching the genitals of the man is the actual illegal act and what gets these women in trouble with LE. So, they may operate in public as legit businesses, but have illegal activity in the backroom. However, a high percentage of providers and mama-sans have internally "LE detectors" that look for signs that the man is really undercover. For example, in New York City, an undercover cop cannot be nude during a massage. Therefore, it is highly unlikely that a provider will perform a lewd act on a man that will not remove his boxers. This actually happened to me, unknowingly, the first time I went to an MP!

Interestingly, it might have been my first. I was a total novice even after doing some research but did all the wrong things. I paid with a credit card, didn't take off my boxers and generally did everything that an undercover cop would do. Obviously she was nervous and wouldn't "do" the things I expected her to do.

About 45 minutes in to the 60 minute session I had to convince her I wasn't a cop by showing her my business card and license. I got my HE, but it was rushed and very expensive. It's good I learned the first time.

As for any more strange experiences, there was an independent provider in LA that worked from her apartment I found from Backpage. She was really into Reiki and all this energy stuff. She didn't give HE, but would rub on you all her "energy"... needless to say that was strange.
TIL a massage parlor is not what I thought it was. Now I don't know what to call a place that gives actual massages. Massage Spa?
